explanation: The failed-mount outcome is called 'read-only'. The code sets Writable=False, which GetWritability maps to NoCommit for this source (170): editing is allowed in memory but never saved (enum comment at 248). That is not read-only. Say that an unmountable hive opens as an empty scratch store the person can edit, with nothing written back. Also state the successful-mount outcome (Writable=True, edits go to the mounted hive and apply when the source is closed, line 137), since the rule claims the whole open.

The unload happens only when the source is a user hive AND its policy object is a registry proxy (110). A hive whose mount failed (71-74) holds a POL scratch store, so closing it takes the 'success without any step' path. 'Closing a mounted user hive source' is right but 'other source types' is wrong for the failed-mount hive; name that case.

The gpt.ini version is raised (UpdateGptIni, 124) before the edition test, so it also happens on editions without Group Policy support; the rule omits it. It also omits where the diff goes: the current user's registry for a user source, the local machine registry for a computer source (130). Add both.
The refresh requested is scoped: RefreshPolicyEx(Not User, 0) refreshes computer policy for a computer source and user policy for a user source. Say which, so a rebuilder does not refresh both.

'Saving a policy source' overreaches. UpdateGptIni is called only when saving the local policy source (124) and a per-user policy source (145); POL file, registry, hive and scratch saves never touch a gpt.ini. Name those two sources. Also, a missing Version line is written as 65537 whatever the section, and a gpt.ini that exists without Version keeps its other lines.

The counts are per matching value, not per match. checkValList adds one for every value of an off or on value list that is present (11-18), so a checkbox with a list can add several tenths of disabled evidence or several present elements; only the single on/off value adds exactly one. Also the off-state weighting is applied only to a checkbox that is not queued for deletion. State the per-value counting.

The three conditions are not alternatives: they are an if / else-if / else chain. The on value list is consulted only when no on value is defined, and the stored-number-equals-1 test only when neither is defined; with an on value defined but absent, a present on value list does not tick the box. Off values and off lists never change the result (it is false either way). Rewrite as precedence.

The merge happens only when exactly two policies in the category share the display name (119); three or more with that name are left alone. Also the user-section copy is not kept separately: the first copy is removed and the second becomes the both-section policy (125-127), and the count of merges is returned. Add the exactly-two condition.

says: No rule for which registry values a policy is taken to reference, used both to list them (GetReferencedRegistryValues) and to forget them. The only rule (forgetting) is stated as removal. Write the referencing rule: the policy's own value, every value of its on/off lists and of checkbox and dropdown-item lists (each list entry using its own key, else the list's key, else the element's or policy's), each non-list element's value, a list element contributing its key as an entry with no value name, duplicates counted once. Other capabilities rely on this set.
